newsitem.title: UK: Hamleys profits up, but toy market flat.
newsitem.headline: Hamleys profits up, but toy market flat.

text.p: British toy store Hamleys Plc said on Tuesday underlying profits rose eight percent last year even though the overall toy market was flat, and lacked any really big sellers to capture shoppers' imaginations.

Hamleys, whose flagship store in London is a big draw for tourists, said pretax profits rose to 6.88 million pounds ($11.1 million) up from 6.38 million. Sales increased to 30.49 million pounds from 30.12 million. The dividend was up 11 percent to nine pence a share.
Chairman Howard Dyer was optimistic about prospects for 1997.

"We remain confident that 1997 will continue the improvement in both the Hamleys' and House of Toys' businesses, although like-for-like sales have started the year in line with last year's," he said in a statement.
But during the key Christmas season the overall market was stagnant.

"I think it was flat (in the UK) in terms of overall sales," he told Reuters in an interview. He said Hamleys market share was up, year on year, but not dramatically and since January sales had eased back.
He said sales were hit by shoppers leaving Christmas buying until the last minute and the absence of any blockbuster toy to lure them in sooner.

"There was nothing really sexy in the marketplace," he said, "Buzz Lightyear (a character from the film 'Toy Story') was the one thing that caught people's imagination over the Christmas period and that was in short supply."
He said merchandise linked to the re-released Star Wars films was looking quite promising for this year - including a Star Wars version of the board game Monopoly.
Dyer said the group's plans to open outlets within Debenhams department stores should improve margins.

Hamleys will open 23 units of its House of Toys' operation at Debenhams centres on a year round basis, with a further 28 units operating during the Christmas period. Debenhams is owned by Burton Group.
